# Active Directory Enumeration

## Machine Account Quota

> MachineAccountQuota (MAQ) is a domain level attribute that by default permits unprivileged users to attach up to 10 computers to an Active Directory (AD) domain ([source](https://blog.netspi.com/machineaccountquota-is-useful-sometimes/))



### Recommendation

From a security stand point it is recommended to set the **MAQ** to zero, as well as remove **NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users** from the local policy "Add workstations to domain".

Reason being that when **MAQ = 0** but the user still has **SeMachineAccountPrivilege** (i.e. being listed in "Add workstations to domain" or has inherited the privilege through control delegations of an OU or group), stale or pre-staged computers can still be joined to the domain without the **MAQ** being touched.

 <main id=main class=site-main role=main>
 <article id=post-4253 class="post-4253 post type-post status-publish format-standard has-post-thumbnail hentry category-microsoft">
 <header class=entry-header style=display:none!important>
 
 
 
 
 
 
 </header>
 
 <div class=entry-content>
 
 <div class=entry-featured style=display:none!important>
 </div>
 
 
<div class=wp-block-jetpack-markdown style=display:none!important>
</div>
<p style=display:none!important>Microsoft Secure Score helps organizations get insights into security posture based on security-related measurements. Microsoft Defender for Identity leverages Secure Score with twenty-seven recommended actions. In a series of blog posts, I will go through all twenty-seven recommended actions of what it means, a plan of approach, their impact, and my security recommendations, hopefully helping others. The one in the series is the “” recommended action.</p>
<h2 class=wp-block-heading style=display:none!important></h2>
<p style=display:none!important>You have twenty-seven recommendations if you filter the Secure Score recommended actions for Microsoft Defender for Identity.</p>
<ul class=wp-block-list style=display:none!important>
</ul>
<p style=display:none!important>Some recommended actions are easy to configure, but others require time, proper planning, auditing, and expertise. This blog post will review the recommended action of “.”</p>
<p style=display:none!important>&nbsp;Microsoft keeps updating the recommended actions list. I will do my best to keep the list up-to-date.</p>
<h2 class=wp-block-heading style=display:none!important></h2>
<p style=display:none!important>The recommendation’s description and title make it unclear which configurations Microsoft is talking about.</p>
<div class=wp-block-image style=display:none!important>
</div>
<p style=display:none!important>You get detailed information about the unsecured domain configurations if there are any exposed entities, though.</p>
<div class=wp-block-image style=display:none!important>
</div>
<p style=display:none!important>Luckily, Microsoft also provides a link in the implementation tab, which gives us more information. What it comes down to is the following.</p>
<ol class=wp-block-list style=display:none!important>
</ol>
<p style=display:none!important>The latter is the easiest of the two. By default, every authenticated user can join ten machines to the domain. Back in the day, it was easier if a user could join a device to the domain, but now that malicious actors&nbsp;&nbsp;this feature, it is wise to limit the machine’s count to zero. If an automated process adds devices to the domain, it has permission to bypass the default limit of ten anyway, so the impact then is presumably very low.</p>
<h3 class=wp-block-heading>Set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to “0”</h3>
<p>Some organizations set the “ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota” property to a high number not to hit the ten-device limit, which is even worse. In any case, I highly recommend setting the “ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota” property to 0. Continue reading if you want to know how.</p>
<p>Before setting the “ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota” property to 0, you can be sure a service account or administrative account can add computers to the domain regardless of changing the “ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota” property to 0. There are two main ways to set the permissions.</p>
<ol class=wp-block-list>
<li>Add a group policy to an organizational unit with the following policy set: Computer Configuration &gt; Windows Settings &gt; Security Settings &gt; Local Policies &gt; User Rights Assignment &gt; Add workstations to Domain.</li>
<li>Create a custom task to delegate using delegation of control and set “Create All Child Objects” for “Computer Objects” for a user or group.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Note</strong>: You can only link Group Policy Objects (GPO) to organizational units. If you want to use the “Computers” container in Active Directory, use option 2.</p>
<p>Here is an example of the policy to add an account to add computer objects to the domain.</p>
<div class=wp-block-image>
<figure class="aligncenter size-full"><img data-attachment-id=4279 data-permalink=https://thalpius.com/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-03/ data-orig-file=https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-03.png data-orig-size=2422,1482 data-comments-opened=1 data-image-meta='{"aperture":"0","credit":"","camera":"","caption":"","created_timestamp":"0","copyright":"","focal_length":"0","iso":"0","shutter_speed":"0","title":"","orientation":"0"}' data-image-title="Microsoft Defender for Identity Recommended Actions Resolve Unsecure Domain Configurations 03" data-image-description data-image-caption data-medium-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-03.png?w=300" data-large-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-03.png?w=720" loading=lazy width=2422 height=1482 src=data:image/png;base64, alt class=wp-image-4279 srcset sizes><figcaption class=wp-element-caption>Image 3: Policy to add an account to add computer objects to the domain</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<p>Here is an example of delegation of control to set permissions for an account to add computer objects to the domain.</p>
<div class=wp-block-image>
<figure class="aligncenter size-full"><img data-attachment-id=4280 data-permalink=https://thalpius.com/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-04/ data-orig-file=https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-04.png data-orig-size=2056,1440 data-comments-opened=1 data-image-meta='{"aperture":"0","credit":"","camera":"","caption":"","created_timestamp":"0","copyright":"","focal_length":"0","iso":"0","shutter_speed":"0","title":"","orientation":"0"}' data-image-title="Microsoft Defender for Identity Recommended Actions Resolve Unsecure Domain Configurations 04" data-image-description data-image-caption data-medium-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-04.png?w=300" data-large-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-04.png?w=720" loading=lazy width=2056 height=1440 src=data:image/png;base64, alt class=wp-image-4280 srcset sizes><figcaption class=wp-element-caption>Image 4: Object type</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<div class=wp-block-image>
<figure class="aligncenter size-full"><img data-attachment-id=4281 data-permalink=https://thalpius.com/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-05/ data-orig-file=https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-05.png data-orig-size=2056,1440 data-comments-opened=1 data-image-meta='{"aperture":"0","credit":"","camera":"","caption":"","created_timestamp":"0","copyright":"","focal_length":"0","iso":"0","shutter_speed":"0","title":"","orientation":"0"}' data-image-title="Microsoft Defender for Identity Recommended Actions Resolve Unsecure Domain Configurations 05" data-image-description data-image-caption data-medium-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-05.png?w=300" data-large-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-05.png?w=720" loading=lazy width=2056 height=1440 src=data:image/png;base64, alt class=wp-image-4281 srcset sizes><figcaption class=wp-element-caption>Image 5: Permissions</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<div class=wp-block-image>
<figure class="aligncenter size-full"><img data-attachment-id=4282 data-permalink=https://thalpius.com/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-06/ data-orig-file=https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-06.png data-orig-size=2056,1440 data-comments-opened=1 data-image-meta='{"aperture":"0","credit":"","camera":"","caption":"","created_timestamp":"0","copyright":"","focal_length":"0","iso":"0","shutter_speed":"0","title":"","orientation":"0"}' data-image-title="Microsoft Defender for Identity Recommended Actions Resolve Unsecure Domain Configurations 06" data-image-description data-image-caption data-medium-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-06.png?w=300" data-large-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-06.png?w=720" loading=lazy width=2056 height=1440 src=data:image/png;base64, alt class=wp-image-4282 srcset sizes><figcaption class=wp-element-caption>Image 6: Delegation of control wizard</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<p>Now that the account responsible for adding computer objects to the domain has the proper permissions, use ADSIEDIT to change the limit to 0 for the “ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota” property. Search for the property “ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota” and change it to 0.</p>
<div class=wp-block-image>
<figure class="aligncenter size-full"><img data-attachment-id=4283 data-permalink=https://thalpius.com/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-07/ data-orig-file=https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-07.png data-orig-size=2310,1362 data-comments-opened=1 data-image-meta='{"aperture":"0","credit":"","camera":"","caption":"","created_timestamp":"0","copyright":"","focal_length":"0","iso":"0","shutter_speed":"0","title":"","orientation":"0"}' data-image-title="Microsoft Defender for Identity Recommended Actions Resolve Unsecure Domain Configurations 07" data-image-description data-image-caption data-medium-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-07.png?w=300" data-large-file="https://thalpius.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/microsoft-defender-for-identity-recommended-actions-resolve-unsecure-domain-configurations-07.png?w=720" loading=lazy width=2310 height=1362 src="data:image/png;base64," alt class=wp-image-4283 srcset sizes><figcaption class=wp-element-caption>Image 7: Setting the “ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota” property</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<p><strong>Note</strong>: If you do not know which account is responsible for adding computer objects to the domain, you can check the event viewer on&nbsp;<em>all</em>&nbsp;domain controllers for event 4741. You can leverage Microsoft Defender for Identity <a href=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/configure-windows-event-collection#configure-audit-policies>auditing</a>, which monitors “Audit Computer Account Management.”</p>
 </div>

### Enumeration

{% tabs %}
{% tab title="PowerShell" %}
**With** [**PowerShell's Active Directory Module**](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/addsadministration/?view=win10-ps)

{% code overflow="wrap" %}
```ps1
Get-ADDomain | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DistinguishedName | Get-ADObject -Properties 'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota'
```
{% endcode %}

**Using** [**PowerSploit**](https://github.com/PowerShellMafia/PowerSploit)

{% code overflow="wrap" %}
```powershell
$Domain = "$env:userdnsdomain"
$LDAP = "DC=" + $Domain.Split(".")
$LDAP = $LDAP -replace " ", ",DC="
(Get-DomainObject -Identity $LDAP -Properties ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota) | Select-Object -ExpandProperty ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota
```
{% endcode %}

**Using native ADSI in PowerShell**

```powershell
$dn = ([ADSI]"LDAP://RootDSE").defaultNamingContext
([ADSI]("LDAP://{0}" -f $dn)).Properties["ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota"][0]
```
{% endtab %}

{% tab title="NetExec" %}
```bash
nxc ldap $DOMAIN_CONTROLLER -d $DOMAIN -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -M maq
```
{% endtab %}
{% endtabs %}
